# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.
I'll explore the codebase to find the transaction labeling logic and the edge-case faults described in the forum digest.

# Transaction Labeling Codebase Report

## 1. Overall Project Structure

Flask microservice for Indian bank statement enrichment (categories, payees, sub-tags, counterparties).

```
/app/
├── Dockerfile                          # gunicorn on :9898
├── .gitignore
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                        # Flask, pandas, fuzzywuzzy, scipy, etc.
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                 # Flask app bootstrap
        ├── Controller.py               # HTTP routes & pipeline orchestration
        ├── BankScripts/                # 35 bank-specific categorizers
        │   ├── Axis.py, HDFC.py, ICICI.py, SBI.py, Kotak.py, ...
        │   └── (one module per bank)
        └── UtilityScripts/
            ├── AppUtil.py              # DF clean + sep_by_* / py_extract helpers
            ├── RegexConstants.py       # Cross-bank subcategory/merchant regexes
            ├── BankRegexConstants.py   # Bank-specific narration patterns
            ├── Purpose.py              # Cross-bank subcategory + merchantType
            ├── CleanName.py            # Merchant name normalization (~2k lines)
            ├── SalaryDetection.py      # Frequency/clustering salary inference
            ├── InternalPayment.py      # Self-transfer detection
            ├── CardPurpose.py / CardCleanNames.py
            ├── PFMCategorization.py    # PFM L1/L2 categories
            ├── SimpleDescription.py
            ├── RecurrentTxns.py
            ├── TransactionCategoryEnums.py
            └── TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py
```

**No test suite exists** (no `test_*`, `*_test.py`, pytest, or unittest files).

---

## 2. End-to-End Labeling Pipeline

**Entry:** `POST /categorizeTransaction` in `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py`

Per bank, the flow is:

1. `AppUtil.clean_input_df` — strip description, coerce amount/balance
2. `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)` — bank script  
   Sets: `transactionCategory`, initial `transactionSubcategory`, `partyName`, `party2`, `merchantType`
3. If `CREDIT_CARD`: `card_clean_names` → `card_purpose`
4. `purpose(transactions, accountType)` — cross-bank subcategory + merchantType
5. `clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)` — merchant name canonicalization
6. If account holder present: `internal_payment(...)`
7. If `SAVING`: `salary_detection(...)`
8. If PFM enabled: `pfm_categorization` → `simple_description`

Default category when nothing matches: **`TRANSFER`**.

---

## 3. Code That Categorizes Transactions

### Primary category (bank scripts)

Each bank module exposes `categorize_<Bank>_transactions`. Pattern: ordered `np.select` on `description` / `remark` / `type` / `amount`.

| Category family | Typical triggers | Example files |
|---|---|---|
| **CHEQUE_DEPOSIT / CHEQUE_PAID** | `CLG`, `CHQ`, `CHEQUE`, all-numeric remark | Axis, HDFC, PNB, Kotak, … |
| **TRANSFER / FUND_TRANSFER / TPT** | residual / FT keywords | all banks (default) |
| **SALARY** (subcategory) | salary keywords or bare numeric codes | Purpose.py, HDFC, Axis |
| **CHEQUE_RETURN / AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE** | return/reject keywords or debit→credit offset | HDFC, ICICI, SCB |
| **REVERSAL / UPI_REVERSAL / IMPS_REVERSAL** | `REV`, `RVSL`, or offsetting credit | most banks |
| **BILL_PAYMENT / PAYMENT_VIA_*** | `BIL/`, BBPS, Razorpay, PayU, etc. | ICICI, HDFC, Indusind |

Key functions:
- Bank: `categorize_HDFC_transactions`, `categorize_ICICI_transactions`, `categorize_Axis_transactions`, …
- Cross-bank subcategory: `purpose()` in `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py`
- Salary inference: `salary_detection()` in `SalaryDetection.py`
- Internal/self: `internal_payment()` in `InternalPayment.py`

### Subcategory (Purpose.py)

`purpose()` applies large regex tables from `RegexConstants.py` for SALARY, LOAN, LOAN_REPAYMENT, INSURANCE, UTILITY_BILL, FOOD_*, TRAVEL, TECHNICAL_BOUNCE, INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE, etc., then clears subcategory for bounce/charges/refund categories.

### Bill transfers

- Category: `BILL_PAYMENT`, `HDFC_BILL_PAYMENT`, `PAYTM_BILL_PAYMENT`, `BBPS_BILL_PAYMENT`, `PAYMENT_VIA_*`
- PFM maps these under `BILL_PAYMENT` (`PFMCategorization.py` lines 51–58, 77)

---

## 4. Payee / Counterparty Extraction

Done **inside each bank script** after category assignment. Output fields:

- `partyName` — cleaned counterparty/merchant
- `party2` — lowercased, space-stripped version of `partyName` (for matching)

Helpers in `AppUtil.py`:

| Helper | Role |
|---|---|
| `sep_by_(desc, n1, n2)` | slash-split segments |
| `sep_by_dash` / `sep_by_colon` / … | other delimiters |
| `py_extract(desc, pat, index)` | regex capture group |

Then `clean_names()` maps thousands of noisy party strings to canonical merchant names (Airtel, Amazon, BESCOM, etc.).

---

## 5. The Four Edge-Case Rules (current logic)

### Edge case A — All-numeric reference strings → cheque deposit

**Rule:** If `remark` (or similar ref field) is only digits of cheque-number length, treat CREDIT as `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` and DEBIT as `CHEQUE_PAID`.

| Bank | File | Pattern | Lines (approx) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Axis | `BankScripts/Axis.py` | `remark ~ ^[0-9]{5,6}$` | 58–59 |
| PNB | `BankScripts/PNB.py` | `remark ~ ^[0-9]{5,6}$` | 60–61 |
| Kotak | `BankScripts/Kotak.py` | `remark ~ ^[0-9]{3,5}$` | 65–67 |
| YES | `BankScripts/YES.py` | `remark ~ ^[0-9]{3,6}$` | 52–53 |
| UCO | `BankScripts/UCO.py` | same as YES | 44–45 |
| BoM | `BankScripts/BankOfMaharashtra.py` | `remark ~ ^[0-9]{5,6}$` | 73–74 |
| RBL | `BankScripts/RBL.py` | `remark ~ ^[0-9]{1,3}$` | 49–50 |
| Karur Vysya | `BankScripts/KarurVyasa.py` | `remark ~ ^00[0-9]{4}$` | 51 |
| Tamilnad Mercantile | `BankScripts/TamilnadMerchantile.py` | `remark ~ ^[0-9]{5,}/` | 33–34 |
| HDFC | `BankScripts/HDFC.py` | 15-char remark `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` | 100 |
| BOB | `BankScripts/BOB.py` | `remark ~ ^[0-9]{3,5}$` (paid) | 70 |

Also narration keywords (`CLG`, `CHQ`, `CHEQUE`, `BY INST`, etc.) across all banks.

---

### Edge case B — Bare numeric code salary credits → salary sub-tag

**Primary explicit rule (HDFC):**

```124:124:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py
[transactions.transactionCategory.eq("TRANSFER") & transactions.description.str.contains("^[0-9]{6}$", na=False, case=False) & transactions.type.eq("CREDIT") & (accountType=="SAVINGS") , "SALARY"],
```

Logic: category already `TRANSFER`, description is **exactly 6 digits**, CREDIT, savings → subcategory `SALARY`.

**Other salary paths:**

1. **Keyword (Purpose.py L14–16):** `SALARY` / `SAL_IMPS` regex on description; CREDIT; not UPI/IMPS; amount > 1000 (some paths); exclude `NOT_SAL`.
2. **Bank-specific:** e.g. Axis `BRN-SALARY PAYMENT-`, `MBSALARY`, `TRANSFER/TB/25-` (Axis.py ~99); HDFC `^A2AINT01`.
3. **Heuristic (`salary_detection`):** cluster party names (Levenshtein), require CREDIT > 2999, exclude UPI/IMPS/reversals/deposits/loans; assign SALARY by mode amount / party frequency vs month count; demote small amounts to REIMBURSEMENT.

There is **no** shared “bare numeric salary” rule outside HDFC’s `^[0-9]{6}$`.

---

### Edge case C — Narration opens with direction words → counterparty extraction

Narrations starting with direction/transfer words are stripped and the remainder becomes `partyName`.

**Representative logic:**

| Pattern | Bank / file | Extraction |
|---|---|---|
| `^TRANSFER TO ` / `^TRANSFER FROM ` | SBI.py 131–132 | strip account digits after TO/FROM |
| `^TRANSFER TO ` | Indusind.py 178; Axis.py 167 | extract after TO |
| `^TRF TO` / `^TRF FROM` / `^TRF FRM` / `^FRM ` | Indusind 181–183; BankOfMaharashtra 169–178 | `py_extract` TO/FROM/FRM |
| `^BY ` / `BY TRF` / `TRANSFER FROM` | CityUnion 130–144; UnionBank 107 | extract after BY/FROM |
| `Received from` / `IMPS Received from` | Paytm 76–82; Kotak 14 | extract name before A/C |
| `ONLINE FUND TRANSFER TO/FROM` | StandardCharted 142–144 | capture group |
| `PAID TO` | Axis 145 | cheque paid beneficiary |
| `NEFT TO ` | HDFC 161 | extract after NEFT TO |
| `TO TRANSFER:` | CityUnion 120 | colon segment |

Cleanup often strips residual direction tokens from `partyName` (e.g. RBL.py 136: strip `TRANSFER TO |^BY |FUND TRANSFER TO`).

---

### Edge case D — Slash-delimited references → payee extraction

**Core helper:** `sep_by_(description, n1, n2)` = join of slash-split segments `[n1:n2]`.

Typical layouts (type/sub-type/ref/payee/…):

| Layout | Bank | Segment used as payee |
|---|---|---|
| `UPI/.../.../payee/...` | Axis, ICICI, SBI, many | index 3 (or 2–5 depending on bank) |
| `IMPS/P2A/ref/.../name` | Axis, Indusind, UCO | index 3–5 |
| `NEFT/.../name` or `NEFT-...-name` | many | slash or dash segment 2–4 |
| `TRF/digits/NAME` | Axis 121 | segment 2 |
| `^[0-9]{5,6}/Name$` | TamilnadMerchantile 69 | segment 1 (name after cheque#) |
| `^[0-9]{3}/...` TRANSFER | PNB 136–138 | segment 1 |
| `^[0-9]{5,}//name` TRANSFER | RBL 125 | segment 2 |
| `BIL/.../...` bill pay | ICICI | various |
| Single `/` TRANSFER | HDFC 201; Axis 146–147 | first or second segment |

HDFC also uses dash-delimited NEFT/IMPS (`sep_by_dash`) heavily; Axis/ICICI prefer slashes.

---

### Edge case E — Offsetting credit after matching debit → bounce vs reversal

**Adjacent-row `shift` logic** (order of rows in the DF matters):

**HDFC** (`HDFC.py` 98–99, 126):

```python
# REVERSAL: CREDIT after DEBIT, same amount, description equals description of row-2,
# and narration contains IMPS|NEFT|UPI|RTGS
type==CREDIT & type.shift(1)==DEBIT & amount==amount.shift(1)
  & description==description.shift(2) & description ~ IMPS|NEFT|UPI|RTGS
  → REVERSAL

# AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE: CREDIT after DEBIT, same amount, same description as previous row
type==CREDIT & type.shift(1)==DEBIT & amount==amount.shift(1)
  & description==description.shift(1)
  → AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE

# Cheque insufficient funds bounce (subcategory):
prev category CHEQUE_PAID & this CHEQUE_RETURN & prev balance < 0
  → INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE
```

**ICICI** (`ICICI.py` 49–50) — cleaner pair:

```python
# same amount + same description as immediate previous DEBIT
+ IMPS|NEFT|UPI|RTGS → REVERSAL
else → AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE
```

**Also:**

| Bank | File | Logic |
|---|---|---|
| Saraswat | Saraswat.py 20 | offsetting + IMPS/NEFT/UPI/RTGS → REVERSAL only |
| Standard Chartered | StandardCharted.py 60 | offsetting + `NACH DR IW` → AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE |
| DCB | DCB.py 16 | offsetting + `^NRTN/CMS` → NEFT_RETURN |

**Keyword bounce/reversal** (when narration says so, without pairing):

- Bounce: `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`, `CHEQUE_RETURN`, `ECS_PENALTY`, `CHEQUE_RETURN_PENALTY`
- Reversal: `REVERSAL`, `UPI_REVERSAL`, `IMPS_REVERSAL`, `ATM_REVERSAL`, `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL`
- Sub-tags in Purpose.py: `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE` / `INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE` via `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE` / `INSUFF_BOUNCE` regexes on cheque-return narrations

**Distinction summary:**  
Same amount + same description after a debit → **bounce** (auto-pay fail) unless narration is a payment rail (IMPS/NEFT/UPI/RTGS) → **reversal**. HDFC’s REVERSAL path compares description to `shift(2)` rather than `shift(1)`.

---

## 6. Key Functions Map

| Concern | Function | Path |
|---|---|---|
| API / orchestration | `categorizeTransaction` | `Controller.py` |
| Bank category + party | `categorize_*_transactions` | `BankScripts/*.py` |
| Subcategory + merchant type | `purpose` | `UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` |
| Merchant cleanup | `clean_names` | `UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` |
| Salary heuristics | `salary_detection` | `UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py` |
| Self transfers | `internal_payment` | `UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py` |
| PFM labels | `pfm_categorization` | `UtilityScripts/PFMCategorization.py` |
| Slash/dash extract | `sep_by_`, `sep_by_dash`, `py_extract` | `UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py` |
| Shared regex | `SALARY`, `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE`, … | `UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` |
| Bank regex | `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN*`, `REVERSAL_*`, … | `UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` |
| Enums | `TransactionCategory`, `TransactionSubcategory` | `UtilityScripts/*Enums.py` |

---

## 7. Tests

**None found.** No unit/integration tests for categorization, payee extraction, bounce/reversal, or salary rules. Validation is effectively live via the Flask API only.

---

## 8. Design Notes Relevant to These Rules

1. **`np.select` is first-match-wins** within each conditions list; rule order is critical (reversals/bounces are usually early; cheque numeric remarks later; default TRANSFER last).
2. **Party extraction is bank-local**, not shared — same narration shape may be handled differently per bank.
3. **`purpose()` runs after bank scripts**, so bank-set subcategory (e.g. HDFC bare-numeric SALARY) can be overridden or refined by Purpose/SalaryDetection.
4. **Offset bounce/reversal assumes chronological row order** matching statement order; no date-window matching across non-adjacent rows (except HDFC’s `shift(2)` description check).
</task_result>
</task>

steps.reasoning_content:
Let me look at the `sep_by_` function more carefully. The join with empty string is suspicious:
The issue is clear now. The `py_extract` call for TRFR narration is grabbing the wrong capture group. The pattern `"TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)"` has two groups: group 0 is the direction word ("TO" or "FROM"), and group 1 is the name. But the 0-index is being passed, so it always returns the direction instead of the name.

For HDFC, the single-group pattern `" To (.*)"` is correct, but the bounce/reversal logic is also broken.
